Documentation Studio turns a Figma page into real documentation — spec sheets, design tokens, annotations and measurements — in one plugin, in Design Mode and Dev Mode.


── WHAT IT DOES ──────────────────────────────────────


DOCS Scan a page and generate documentation three ways: a doc page with a

cover, contents and a section per component; one full spec sheet per component;

or a compact summary board.


SPECS Per-component spec sheets with Anatomy, Properties, Variants, Styling

and Layout & spacing — per-layer padding, gaps and sizes colour-coded like

Figma's inspector. Handoff mode adds measured dimensions and annotations

around a clean copy of any frame.


TOKENS Generate real Figma variable collections — colour, typography, spacing,

radius — from 14 open-licensed base libraries (Tailwind, Material, Radix, Open

Color, Ant, Fluent, IBM Carbon, Atlassian, Polaris, Uber Base, Bootstrap,

Chakra UI, GitHub Primer, Nord) or your own base colours. Ramps are generated

with an OKLCH engine for even perceptual steps, with Light + Dark modes,

semantic aliasing and bound text styles. Or document the tokens you already

have, on canvas.


USAGE Inventory every component instance and audit its health: overrides,

hidden instances, renamed layers, local-vs-library components and hardcoded

fills. Click any instance to jump straight to it.


ANNOTATIONS Native Figma annotations — they live on the layer, move with it,

carry Figma's own categories and show live property values in Dev Mode.


MEASURE Native Figma measurements in Dev Mode; drawn overlays with outlines

and guides in Design Mode. Padding, gaps and sizes, with reusable presets.


EXPORT Export the whole system as Markdown or HTML.


── WHY THIS ONE ──────────────────────────────────────


• One plugin for the whole documentation lifecycle, not one slice of it.

• Uses Figma's native annotation and measurement APIs, so your notes and

measurements stay live instead of becoming stale drawings.

• Token generation is included, not gated.

• Runs entirely on your machine. No account, no sign-in, no uploads — the

plugin requests no network access at all.


── GETTING STARTED ───────────────────────────────────


1. Open the plugin on a page with components.

2. Hit Scan on the Docs tab.

3. Pick an output format and Generate.


Everything lands to the right of your existing page content, selected and

ready to move.

Preparing formal style guide documentation from your local styles (and keeping it updated!) has always felt like double entry to me. But thanks to the Figma API you can now prepare a presentable style guide for clients & developers with a click of a button.

Generate Color Swatches

Generate A Style Guide

model.description:
Change one base variable — every dependent color, spacing and type value updates itself.


Dynamic Variables lets your Figma variables derive from each other: write a small JavaScript formula in a variable's description field, and the plugin keeps its value in sync with everything it depends on.

🎨 primary-600: {{ cd($base-color).darken(0.1) }} — correct today, correct after every rebrand.


You know the ritual: the brand color shifts, and now it's 20 shades × light-and-dark modes of hand edits — and the one shade you miss is the one that ships. Type scale tweak? Same ritual. Spacing rhythm? Same. Your tokens already depend on each other — Figma just doesn't know it yet. This plugin is how you tell it.

🛝 Try it before installing: the documentation runs every example live in your browser — editable variables, editable expressions, visual previews. Two minutes there and you'll know if this is for you.

  1. 🤖 AI-assisted editing: click Copy Brief for AI, paste it into ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini — whatever assistant you already use — describe what you want in plain words, then paste the reply back. The plugin parses it and shows a preview of every change before anything touches your variables — it can update expressions and even create the variables it needs. Or hand the brief straight to the Figma Agent, which edits your variables directly. No API key, no extra subscription.
  2. 🖥️ Visual editor: browse collections as a tree and edit expressions in a real code editor (Monaco — the engine inside VS Code) with syntax highlighting, autocomplete for your variable names, and inline errors, instead of squinting at description fields.
  3. 🧩 Global Functions: define a helper once — say, a function that picks readable text for any background — and call it from any expression. Repeated logic lives in one place.
  4. 🗂️ Relative paths, on by default: $('./Base') reads a sibling, $('../radius') reads one group up — so one generic expression serves a whole family of tokens and survives renames of the family itself.
  5. 🏃 Motion variables: Figma's new Timing & Easing types are supported — switch easing curves by condition (reduced motion, brand, platform) via alias selection, and export any curve as CSS with cssEasing().


🔑 How it works:


  1. ⚙️ Expressions: any JavaScript between {{ }} in a variable's description. Reference siblings as $A, other collections as $('Collection/Variable'). A variable C defined as {{ $A + $B }} updates whenever A or B changes.

PLUGIN CRAFTED FOR REFOKUS


Plugin Documentation

This plugin extracts font-related properties from your local text styles and converts them into reusable variables. It automatically applies the following variables:

•Font size

•Font weight

•Font family


Additionally, the plugin documents—but does not apply—the following properties:

•Line height

•Letter spacing


This is due to a current Figma limitation: dynamic variables for these properties are not yet supported. As a workaround, these values are stored as string variables for documentation purposes only.


For example:

If the original line-height is 100%, the plugin will store it as a variable with:

variableName: 100%, variableValue: 1em (calculated as 100 ÷ 100 × 1em)


Naming Convention for text styles:


To ensure accurate detection and conversion, your text styles should follow this naming structure:

•Use the prefix title- followed by a number (e.g., title-1) for headings

•Use the prefix text- followed by a number (e.g., text-2) for paragraphs


You can also use suffixes to describe combo classes. For instance:

•text-2-buttonLabel


This will still be recognized as a text-2 style with additional contextual information.

– Flexible Selection: Begin by selecting any component, component set, component instance, or design element like frames or shapes. – Comprehensive Documentation: If no specific selection is made, the plugin will catalog all component sets and components throughout your file. It may take longer if your file includes numerous components with multiple variations.


The plugin is designed to efficiently handle large datasets to prevent freezing during rendering. However, if rendering all showcases becomes overly time-consuming, consider using the component-by-component rendering option for a quicker and more manageable process.


– Theme-Specific Documentation: For files containing multiple themes, the plugin generates themed documentation frames. For 'Dark' themes, components are displayed against a black background, while other themes use a light gray background.

You can adjust these backgrounds, including setting them to transparent, to suit your project needs. Once you modify these color settings, the plugin will remember your preferences and apply these settings in all subsequent operations, ensuring consistency across your documentation process.


– Rendering Options: You can choose to display the component showcases directly on the active page, where a new frame will appear at the top of your layer list. Alternatively, opt for documentation on a newly created page, where the plugin will generate a timestamped page at the bottom of your page list.


– Detailed Property Display: The plugin renders a table for properties that have multiple values, ensuring detailed visual documentation. Properties with only a single value are neatly listed below the table, providing a clear and organized overview. At the end of each table, a timestamp indicates when the showcase was rendered. Additionally, if a component has a description, it will also be displayed.


– Testing your components: For components that lack variants or have errors, I display "N/A" in the cell instead of the component, allowing you to easily test for missing variants. Keep in mind that the absence of some variants is normal, as they may not always be necessary.


As a testing tool, you can also change the background color in all cells simultaneously, visually testing how all your components and their variants appear against different backgrounds. This feature enhances the ability to ensure visual consistency across your designs.

– Theme-Specific Rendering: The plugin facilitates rendering components against different themes, making it easy to test and compare visual consistency across various backgrounds.


– Efficiency Boost: Save valuable design time by generating demonstrations for components directly within Figma. This feature helps you understand how your assets function, identify missing elements, and provide clear visualizations that save development time—ensuring design integrity.


– Dynamic Updates: Re-run the plugin at any time to refresh your documentation as your designs evolve, ensuring your component overviews always reflect the latest changes.

model.name: Color Kitchen
model.description:
Create recipes for working with colors, color variables and styles systematically, directly on the canvas where you can see what's happening.


Demo file


How to

  1. Run Create components to create a page with components needed for the Color Kitchen plugin
  2. Place instances of the Color Kitchen Recipe component on your canvas.
  3. Select a color, color variable or a color style as source by applying it to the first ⚪️ Swatch Layer on the left side.
  4. Change the ⚙️ Modifier components and the modifiers 🎚 Value as you please. You can also detach the recipe to be able to move things around more freely within the recipe. Add as many ⚙️ Modifiers and ⚙️Color Swatches as you want.
  5. Select one or more recipes and Run recipes to see the modifiers changing all the color swatches on their right. Or run all recipes on the page by not selecting anything before running the command.
  6. If you want to link two or more variables or styles create or apply existing variables or styles to one or more ⚪️ Swatch Layers on the right side.


Additional features

  1. Add ⚙️Print instances to the recipe to see color values, contrast ratios, variable and style names or descriptions printed on the canvas.
  2. Change the variant properties of ⚙️Color Swatch layers to override specific color values in styles with multiple fills, effects and gradients. You need to specify which of the effects, fills or color stops in a gradient you want to override by providing the coordinates as a number. 0 is the first fill/effect. In the case of gradients you need to provide two numbers, the number of the fill and the number of the color stop, like that: 0:1


Use cases

  1. Variation: Link multiple variables or styles with varying opacity or luminance to one main variable or style.
  2. Inheritance: I.e. link colors in shadows or gradients to your main color variables or styles.
  3. Exploration: Try different treatments and color models to create palettes.
  4. Documentation & Collaboration: Make color choices traceable and reproducible.
  5. Theming: Make all colors dependent on a few accent colors.


Available color transformations

  1. Brighten/darken
  2. Saturate/desaturate
  3. Channels: Set or modify a value of a single channel (i.e. red or hue or lightness)
  4. Opacity: Set or add to/subtract from opacity
  5. Luminance: Set to make contrasts work
  6. Mix two colors
  7. Blend two colors using different blend modes
  8. Contrast Minimum: Darken or brighten, until the given contrast ratio in relation to a given second color is met. (Ignores opacity)


Sources

  1. Most color functions are using chroma-js, check the docs for more information.
  2. Color extraction from images uses extract-colors and color-thief.
  3. Alternative color mixing function uses spectral-js.
  4. Built with Create Figma Plugin by Yuan Qing Lim
  5. Node Decoder by Gavin Mc Farland was a huge help


Roadmap

  1. Modifiers to work with additional useful color models like HSLuv or Material Designs' HCT
  2. Generate new styles in addition to syncing existing ones
  3. Cooking with noodles: Use prototyping links or maybe FigJam's connectors to connect color swatches
  4. Add support for variables
  5. Additional guidance within the component descriptions.
  6. More comfortable ways to use a color for multiple shadows
  7. Add demo file
  8. Modifiers that ensure a certain contrast threshold minimum against a selected background color.
  9. Add label elements that print color values and style names to the canvas for readability

The Complete Bidirectional Design System Engine — Variables, Styles, and Data Extraction at Once!!


Figma plugin that synchronizes your entire design system between Markdown and Figma.

Create Variables & Styles from MD, or export your existing Figma system back to MD — with smart bindings and zero configuration.

1. AI Workflow Optimization: Instantly import AI-generated DESIGN.md files into Figma for free. Build large-scale design systems without wasting AI tokens (MCP).

2. True Bidirectional Sync: Precisely export complex Variables and Styles built in Figma back into clean, organized Markdown documentation.

3. Semantic Design Preservation: Even if custom fonts are missing from your system, your original 'design intent' is permanently preserved in Variables, while screens safely render using fallback fonts.


[AI / Figma MCP / Documentation] ⇄ DESIGN.md ⇄ [MD to Figma(Free, Instant, and Bidirectional!)] ⇄ [Figma Variables & Styles]


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━


✨ What's New in v2.0.2


1. Normalized Naming Compatibility (Fuzzy Match)

Slash (/) vs. Dash (-): Solves naming rule discrepancies between Figma's grouping slash (`/`) and developers' coding dash (`-`). It matches variables normalized in memory to run Smart Updates, preserving your original Figma folder structures.


2. Fully Partitioned MD Export

Primitive & Semantic Separation: Color, Spacing, and Radius variables are now exported into cleanly separated Primitive and Semantic tables to align perfectly with standard design system templates.


3. Multi-Mode & Typography Values Tracking

Light/Dark Mode Colors: Semantic colors are exported with both Light and Dark mode columns.

Dynamic Typography Resolution: Text styles retrieve values directly from their bound variables during export, ensuring any modifications in Figma are immediately captured.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━


🚀 What Gets Generated


Variables (4 Collections)

Colors: Primitive palette + Semantic aliases (Light/Dark mode). Strict alias-binding enforced.

Spacing & Radius: Primitive scales + Semantic aliases.

Typography: fontSize, lineHeight, letterSpacing grouped intuitively (Display, Body, etc.).


Styles (100% Bound to Variables)

Color Styles → bound to Semantic Color Variables

Text Styles → bound to Typography Variables

Effect Styles → drop shadows bound to Spacing Variables

Grid Styles → columns, rows bound to Spacing Variables


Partial Sync & Selective Generation

Already have Variables? Generate Styles only — the plugin auto-links them without recreating anything. Use the checkboxes to update only what you need.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━


📖 How It Works


1. Collect your design system data — from a Figma file, brand guidelines, website, or any source.

2. Download the `DESIGN-TEMPLATE.md` from the plugin.

3. Hand both to any AI (Claude, ChatGPT, etc.) — the AI uses the template as a pattern reference to organize your data.

4. Paste the AI-generated DESIGN.md into the plugin.

5. Select which Variables and Styles to generate.

6. Click Generate — done. (Use **Export** to extract it back later!)


(Includes: DESIGN.md Template & AI Prompt Guide inside the plugin)


=================================

📦 MD to Figma

✨ v2.0.2 핵심 업데이트


1. 네이밍 호환성 최적화 (Fuzzy Match)

슬래시(/)와 하이픈(-) 호환: 피그마의 그룹핑용 슬래시(`/`)와 개발 코드용 하이픈 (`-`) 기호 차이를 매칭 시 메모리 내에서 정규화하여 대조합니다. 기존에 피그마 내에 설정된 원래 이름과 폴더 구조를 해치지 않고 값만 안전하게 업데이트합니다.

3. 다중 모드 및 타이포그래피 추적

다중 모드 색상: 세맨틱 컬러의 Light 모드와 Dark 모드 값을 동시에 추출하여 양방향 테이블 형태로 내보냅니다.

🚀 생성되는 항목


Variables (4개 컬렉션)

Colors: Primitive 팔레트 + Light/Dark 모드 Semantic Alias (HEX 직접 입력 차단, 참조 강제)

Typography: 폰트 사이즈, 행간, 자간 등 (Display, Body 등 섹션별 자동 그룹핑)


Styles (Variables 완벽 연동)

Color Styles → Semantic Color Variables 연동

Text Styles → Typography Variables 연동

Effect Styles → dropshdow 숫자 값 Spacing Variables 연동

Grid Styles → gutter/margin 숫자 값 Spacing Variables 연동


선택적 생성 및 부분 등록 (Partial Sync)

이미 Variables가 있다면 Styles만 생성할 수 있습니다. 기존 변수를 덮어쓰지 않고 지능적으로 연결합니다. 체크 박스로 원하는 항목만 업데이트하세요.


━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━


📖 사용 방법


1. 디자인 시스템 데이터를 수집합니다. Figma 파일, 브랜드 가이드라인, 웹사이트 또는 모든 출처에서 수집하세요.

2. 플러그인에서 'DESIGN-TEMPLATE.md '을 다운로드합니다.

3. 여러분들의 AI(클로드, ChatGPT 등)에게 두 가지를 모두 건네주세요. AI는 템플릿을 패턴 참조로 사용하여 데이터를 정리합니다.

4. AI가 템플릿화하여 정리한 DESIGN.md 를 플러그인에 붙여넣기.

5. 생성할 변수와 스타일을 선택합니다.

6. 생성! ( 내보내기를 사용하여 나중에 DS추출 가능 )

GitFig connects your Figma files directly to GitHub repositories: bi-directional sync and version control for your

design system.


HOW IT WORKS


Connect any GitHub repository you have access to, or create a new one from inside the plugin

Map JSON token files to Figma Variables, Color styles, Text styles, or Effect styles

Pull tokens from GitHub to create or update Variables and Styles

Commit the changes you check and push them to GitHub, or open a pull request


VARIABLE MODES (FREE DURING THE PREVIEW)


Sync every mode of your variable collections (light/dark, multi-brand, density) in both directions using mode-keyed

token files: root keys are mode names, and every mode shares the same token structure. One variable gets one value per

mode on pull, never duplicates. Per-mode change detection shows exactly which mode changed.


Variable modes sync is free for everyone during the v1.3 preview. It becomes part of GitFig Pro, a paid plan, in a

future release; pricing will be announced before that happens, and you can opt in to a one-time launch heads-up inside

the plugin. The core workflow stays free.


Note: modes per collection are limited by your Figma plan. The Figma Starter plan allows one mode per collection, so

multi-mode sync requires a paid Figma plan.


GIT-STYLE WORKFLOW


GitFig detects changes to your Variables and Styles within seconds and lists them with checkboxes.

Changes: every edit, per mode, with the old and new value a hover away

Commit: exactly the changes you check, with a message (the first line is the subject)

Ready to push: review your commits, then push them to GitHub in one atomic commit

Pull asks before overwriting edits you have not committed, and every pull can be undone in one step.


FEATURES


Bi-directional sync between Figma and GitHub

Variable modes: sync all modes of a collection in one file

Styles sync both ways: color, text, and effect styles import on pull and export on push

Alias references round-trip as readable {Collection.path.to.token} references

Your metadata is safe: pushes preserve $extensions and other custom $-metadata in your repo

Multi-file push: each mapping writes its own file, all in one atomic commit

Safe by default: GitFig warns before you push over unpulled commits or pull over uncommitted edits

Branch support: switch branches, create new ones, open pull requests from Figma

New repositories start with starter primitives, a light/dark semantic collection, and color and text styles

Supports W3C Design Tokens, Style Dictionary, and Tokens Studio formats

Cross-device: create commits on one device, push from another

Readable, resizable UI with zoom (Ctrl/Cmd +, -, 0)


PERFECT FOR


Design systems teams managing tokens in code

Teams maintaining light/dark or multi-brand themes

Designers who want version control for their work

Teams using GitHub for design-developer handoff


RESOURCES


Website: gitfig.com

Documentation: docs.gitfig.com (guides, tutorials, reference)

Community: github.com/ds1/gitfig-community (announcements, support, discussion)


SPREAD THE LOVE


Leave a Like (heart) and share the plugin to help others discover GitFig.

Documentation & Video Tutorials


For plugin documentation and step by step video tutorials, please visit https://docs.hypermatic.com/copydoc


Questions & Support


CopyDoc is still a baby panda, so if you notice any bugs or have any questions about the plugin, please get in touch directly via https://hypermatic.com/contact and we'll help you troubleshoot and resolve them as quickly as possible.


Security


CopyDoc is designed to be privacy and security focused — for details about security and how the plugin works, please visit https://docs.hypermatic.com/copydoc/security


Features


  1. Privacy focused — no data or content ever leaves your Figma file.
  2. Export Figma text layers to XLSX, DOCX, CSV, Markdown and JSON files directly to your computer (or to Airtable).
  3. Bulk update Figma text layers via XLSX, DOCX, CSV, Markdown or JSON import directly from your computer (or from Airtable).
  4. Create a custom content library inside your Figma file, with optional Google Sheets, Airtable and Figma Variable integrations.
  5. Sync repeating text/image content or CSS styles from a Google Sheet or XLSX/CSV file.
  6. Automatically generate Figma data tables from a Google Sheet or XLSX/CSV.
  7. Seamless design localization and translations via OpenAI, Claude, Gemini or Excel (XLSX) spreadsheet export/import.
  8. Find & Replace feature to quickly update any matching text.
  9. Automatically generate Charts by adding your own spreadsheet data.
  10. Export frames to DOCX, XLSX, TXT, EPUB, HTML or PDF.
  11. Quickly export selected text layers to XLSX, DOCX, CSV, Markdown, JSON or XLIFF files.
  12. Spell check your Figma text in dozens of languages.
  13. Download all Figma comments to CSV and JSON files.
  14. Include design references for text and comment exports.


Batch export/import Figma text content with one click.

Export every text layer in your design to Excel (XLSX), CSV, DOCX, Markdown or JSON files with one click, then instantly re-import any updated text content from the edited file back into Figma.


Privacy and security focused — nothing ever leaves your Figma file.

CopyDoc doesn’t upload, store or process any Figma data outside of the plugin, everything happens securely inside your Figma file, and any exported files are downloaded directly to your computer.


Sync repeatable Figma layer text and image content from spreadsheets with one click.

Easily sync repeating text content (or layer names), image/video content or CSS styles to your Figma layers from any spreadsheet, or automatically generate a table in Figma — just drop an Excel (XLSX) file, CSV file or paste a Google Sheets or Airtable link.


Create your own text expander content library.

Easily create a content library directly inside CopyDoc with snippets expandable via '//' shortcuts or with one-click. Optionally extensible with Google Sheets, Figma Variables and Airtable integrations, and also includes a broad library of realistic placeholder data (or classic Lorem Ipsum).


Seamless text localization and translations

Translate all your UX copy via OpenAI, Claude, Gemini or Excel (XLSX) spreadsheet export/import to easily create new languages for your Figma designs.


Find and replace any text content in your Figma layers.

Quickly find and replace any text content in your Figma designs to save time manually changing the same word across all your layers..


Spell check and fix typos in Figma with one click.

Check your designs for embarrassing spelling mistakes (in dozens of languages) before exporting your text or sharing designs with stakeholders.


Export your Figma designs to popular document formats.

Export your Figma frames to Microsoft Word (.docx), Microsoft Excel (.xlsx), E-Book (.epub), Plain Text (.txt) or PDF files.


CopyDoc Pro


10 free trials of CopyDoc Pro are included with the free version, and if you're a casual user, you can continue using the free version of CopyDoc forever.


If you're a power user, you can optionally upgrade to continue using all the extra features that are only available in the pro version of CopyDoc.


To learn more about CopyDoc Pro, please visit https://www.hypermatic.com/copydoc/#pro
